title: AI in software engineering at Google: Progress and the path ahead
summary: Google describes its internal AI coding features (completion, review-comment resolution, paste adaptation) and the lessons on UX integration, review cost, and data.

assertions.quote: assisting in the completion of 50% of code characters
the code author increasingly becomes a reviewer
Experiments requiring the user to remember to trigger the feature have failed to scale.

verdicts.note: Consistent with Google's internal A/B results and with general UX evidence on defaults and friction, though mostly reported by the vendor.

Google: inline code completion is the most popular AI dev application because its UX feels natural in the IDE (38% acceptance, 67% of code characters AI-assisted); consistent but not a controlled inline-vs-triggered comparison.

assertions.quote: offline metrics are often only rough proxies of user value
The training data is an aligned corpus of code with task-specific annotations in input as well as in output.
improvements to these surfaces can directly impact developer productivity and satisfaction
